'''Kathy Lischke''' (earlier '''Kathy Pierce'''; Decipher message boards: '''klischke''') was a Star Wars CCG tournament director in Northern Virginia.<ref name="kp-people">[http://rothko.decipher.com/starwars/playeractivities/people/index.html Star Wars Customizable Card Game: People Like You], Decipher (March 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19970327211740/http://rothko.decipher.com:80/starwars/playeractivities/people/index.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="kp-thrill">[http://www.decipher.com/newsandhighlights/kathytourneystory.html "The Thrill of Tournament Play"], Kathy Pierce, Decipher NewsFlash (22 January 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19970607131145/http://www.decipher.com:80/newsandhighlights/kathytourneystory.html Internet Archive]</ref> She covered [[DecipherCon 1999]] for Decipher, posting five reports to the DecipherCon: Event Report Board from 11 to 13 November 1999.<ref name="kl-erb">[http://calder.decipher.com/cgi-bin/msgbd?dconerb DecipherCon: Event Report Board] (message list), Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001120101400/http://calder.decipher.com:80/cgi-bin/msgbd?dconerb Internet Archive]</ref> She playtested the [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]] (2001).<ref name="jkrules">[http://www.decipher.com/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt ''Jedi Knights'' Trading Card Game rulebook (credits)], Decipher (2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010820125115/http://www.decipher.com:80/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt Internet Archive]</ref> In 1997 she was engaged to [[Tom Lischke]], Decipher's new Rebel Base Leader<ref name="kp-people" />, and by 2000 she was his wife.<ref name="stackpole">[http://www.stormwolf.com/essays/decipher.html Visiting Decipher], Michael A. Stackpole, stormwolf.com (September 2000 visit). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20250608214406/http://www.stormwolf.com/essays/decipher.html Internet Archive]</ref>

== Tournament director ==

Decipher's 1997 "People Like You" page called Kathy Pierce "a Star Wars tournament director".<ref name="kp-people" /> On 19 January 1997 she directed a three-round Swiss Star Wars CCG tournament at Destiny Comics in Fairfax, Virginia. It drew 30 players and was won by Jeffrey Glazer. Half of the entry fees went to Children's Hospital. Her fiancé Tom Lischke filled in to avoid byes and checked rulings.<ref name="kp-thrill" />

== DecipherCon 1999 reports ==

Her reports covered the Star Wars CCG side of the convention. On Thursday she described the last-minute open qualifier. Light Side Force-denial decks there started with [[Yavin 4: Massassi Throne Room]] and [[Careful Planning]], and used a swamp to pull [[Nudj]]. She also noted many objective decks, among them [[Hunt Down And Destroy The Jedi / Their Fire Has Gone Out Of The Universe|Hunt Down And Destroy The Jedi]], and [[Battle Plan]] as the most common Endor card.<ref name="kl-nudj" />

On Friday she reported [[Joe Alread]]'s win in the [[DecipherCon 1999 Iron Man|Star Wars Ironman tournament]], where lost cards went into a shredder. The [[DecipherCon 1999 Japanese Sealed Deck|Japanese Sealed Deck]] tournament that evening drew more than 140 players.<ref name="kl-iron" /><ref name="kl-jsd" /> On Saturday she named [[Steven Lewis]] and [[Gary Carman]] as the two finalists of the [[1999 Decipher World Championship]]. Carman had lost his planned decks and built two new ones that morning.<ref name="kl-final" /><ref name="kl-necessity" />

== Other Decipher work ==

Lischke was one of the 31 playtesters credited in the ''Jedi Knights'' rulebook.<ref name="jkrules" /> Four Decipher employees set a Guinness World Record on 25–27 May 2002 with a 32-hour ''[[The Lord of the Rings Trading Card Game]]'' marathon. Lischke was among those who brought them food during the weekend.<ref name="marathon">[http://decipher.com/lordoftherings/worldrecords/091202marathon.html Decipher Team Sets Guinness World Record With The Lord of the Rings TCG!], Decipher (September 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20021017115834/http://decipher.com:80/lordoftherings/worldrecords/091202marathon.html Internet Archive]</ref>
